metadata.name: df
metadata.description: Display disk space usage of file systems

installation.note: df is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: df (disk free) displays information about disk space usage of mounted file systems. It shows total space, used space, available space, and usage percentage for each file system. Essential for monitoring disk usage and preventing disk full errors.

syntax.description: Display disk space for all mounted file systems. If FILE or DIRECTORY is specified, shows space for the file system containing that path.

options.description: Display sizes in human-readable format (KB, MB, GB)
options.use_case: Show disk space in readable format (most common usage)
See file system types (ext4, xfs, tmpfs, etc.)

options.description: Display inode usage instead of block usage
options.use_case: Check inode usage (useful when disk shows space but can't create files)

options.description: Include pseudo, duplicate, and inaccessible file systems
options.use_case: Show all file systems including system ones

examples.title: Check disk space (human-readable)
examples.description: Display disk space in readable format
examples.output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda1        20G  8.5G   10G  46% /
/dev/sda2       100G   45G   50G  45% /home
tmpfs           2.0G     0  2.0G   0% /dev/shm

output_explanation.format: Table showing file system disk usage

breakdown.format: Device name (e.g., /dev/sda1) or special file system (tmpfs)

elements.meaning: Mount point (directory where file system is mounted)

output_explanation.notes: Most common usage: df -h. Shows disk space in readable format. Watch Use% - above 80% is getting full.

examples.use_case: Quickly check available disk space on all file systems

examples.title: Check specific directory
examples.description: Check disk space for file system containing /home
examples.output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda2       100G   45G   50G  45% /home

elements.meaning: Shows disk space for file system containing this path

breakdown.useful: Check space for specific directory or mount point
breakdown.common: Often used: df -h / to check root partition

output_explanation.notes: Shows disk space for the file system containing the specified path. Useful for checking specific partitions.

examples.use_case: Check disk space for a specific directory or partition

examples.title: Check inode usage
examples.description: Display inode usage instead of disk space
examples.output:
Filesystem      Inodes  IUsed   IFree IUse% Mounted on
/dev/sda1      5.2M    1.2M    4.0M   23% /

breakdown.useful: Check if you've run out of inodes (can't create files even with space)
breakdown.problem: If IUse% is 100%, you can't create files even if disk has space

output_explanation.notes: Shows inode usage. If IUse% is 100%, you can't create files even if disk has space. Rare but important to check.

examples.use_case: Troubleshoot 'no space' errors when disk shows available space

misconceptions.title: df shows file sizes
misconceptions.misconception: df displays sizes of individual files
misconceptions.reality: df shows file SYSTEM disk usage, not individual file sizes. Use du for directory/file sizes, ls -lh for file sizes.
misconceptions.tip: df = file system space. du = directory/file sizes. ls -lh = individual file sizes.

common_pitfalls.description: df output in blocks is hard to read
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use df -h for human-readable format (KB, MB, GB). Much easier to understand.

common_pitfalls.description: Not monitoring disk usage until it's too late
common_pitfalls.solution: Monitor Use% regularly. Above 80% is getting full, above 90% is critical. Clean up files or expand disk.

related_commands.relationship: Directory sizes; df shows file system space, du shows directory sizes
related_commands.description: Show disk usage of directories and files (complements df)

related_commands.relationship: File sizes; df shows system space, ls shows file sizes
related_commands.description: List files with sizes (ls -lh shows individual file sizes)

best_practices: Always use df -h for human-readable output
Monitor disk usage regularly (check Use% column)
Use df -h / to check root partition
Use df -i if you can't create files despite having space
performance_tips: df -h is the most common usage

additional_notes.human_readable: Always use -h flag for readable output (KB, MB, GB instead of blocks)
additional_notes.usage_percentage: Watch Use% column - above 80% is getting full, above 90% is critical
additional_notes.inodes: Use df -i if you can't create files despite having disk space (inode exhaustion)
additional_notes.common_usage: Most common: df -h (check all), df -h / (check root), df -h /home (check home partition)
